ops.title: Session guard does not read an xargs placeholder as a command name
ops.description:
`<anything> | xargs -I{} {} kill-server` returns no verdict from the session guard, though it runs `tmux kill-server` when the pipe feeds it `tmux`. The guard reads the xargs call and does not treat the replace-string in command position as a name chosen at run time, the way `opaque_command_name` treats `$(...)` there.

Observed 2026-10-11 through the dispatch engine at captain-hook `4f30679a`, with cc-transcript 14.40.1 and again with 14.40.0, so it predates the `command -v` lookup fix (#355):

- `echo tmux | xargs -I{} {} kill-server`: no verdict
- `which tmux | xargs -I{} {} kill-server`: no verdict
- `command -v tmux | xargs -I{} {} kill-server`: no verdict
- `command -v orca | xargs -I{} {} terminal close --terminal t`: no verdict

For contrast, `$(command -v pkill) -f x` is denied as a command named at run time, `command -v reboot | sh` as a shell on stdin, and `eval "$(command -v tmux) kill-server"` as evaluated text. Replay output: `~/.claude/scratch/orca-remote-managed/capt-hook-remote-3/guard-replay-4f30679a.txt`.

Whether the guard should cover this is the owner's call: it changes what the guard protects. Found by lane capt-hook-remote-3 as a second reader of #355; not fixed there.

ops.text: An inline test in sessions.py blocks `echo tmux | xargs -I{} {} kill-server`, or the owner rules the shape out of scope
